catalog_quote: Emai is a minor language in the Edoid group (Elugbe 1989). It is spoken in over 10 villages with approximately 20-25,000 speakers. A tonal language, Emai shows lexical and grammatical tones high (ˊ), low (ˋ), and downstep high (ˊ'). Its morphological template for the basic verb is X-stem-Y. X identifies a persistive qualifier prefix and Y encompasses contrasting perfective/ imperfective toneme suffixes. Tones from these suffixes spread onto lexically toneless verbs. The imperfective suffix is a floating low tone. Traces of perfective suffix -í and its high tone are evident in simple clauses with an intransitive verb or a monotransitive verb whose direct object has left dislocated. ... [p. 262] Orthographic conventions reflect those in Schaefer and Egbokhare (1999; 2007; 2017), where o represents a half open back vowel, e a half open front vowel, and vb a voiced bilabial approximant. new_statements.rule_in_words: Emai (the described lect of Emai-Iuleha-Ora, of which Ihievbe is a section) is a tone language with lexical and grammatical H, L and downstepped H; nouns carry lexical tone, verbs are lexically toneless and take tone from aspect suffixes. The authors say nothing about word stress or accent in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: none (verbs and personal pronouns are toneless/construction-dependent per Egbokhare 1989 fn.3)
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical/grammatical tone at word and clause level in Emai; no stress domain is described. Applies to Ihievbe only by virtue of Glottolog/Ethnologue treating Ihievbe as a section of the same language.
new_statements.identity_note: ihie1238 Ihievbe [ihi] is a Glottolog Bookkeeping entry: 'rather a section of the Emai-Iuleha-Ora [ema] language' (emai1241; Glottolog cites Elugbe 1989:16, Jungraithmayr & Ganslmayr 1986:34, Lewis 2013:95-96). Older Ethnologue editions (2005, 2009) instead filed Ihievbe under North-Central Edoid, Ghotuo-Uneme-Yekhee. Egbokhare 2011:67-69 lists Ihievbe among lects Elugbe left unclassified and reports Oyakhire 1997's dialect group A = Emai, Ihievbe, Ora, Iuleha, Ievbu, Uokha, Urore, Ohami, Sobe; the Emai dictionary glosses Ihievbe as the village 'immediately northeast of Emailand'. The quoted statement describes the Emai lect (Schaefer & Egbokhare's fieldwork variety, Afuze area), not Ihievbe speech itself; no Ihievbe-specific description exists. If catalogued, the entry should be keyed to emai1241 (or flagged as inherited from it).

sources.note: p.234: Emai is 'a tonal language' with lexical and grammatical tones H, L and downstepped H; verbs lexically toneless, receiving aspect-suffix tones; orthography note: acute = high, grave = low, acute+apostrophe = downstepped high. No mention of stress or accent.
